evaluations.evidence: create a new game by entering a name and an optional description
evaluations.rationale: The required inputs (name, optional description) and outcome (new game) are clear with no materially different interpretations.

evaluations.evidence: invite estimators by giving them a URL where they can access the game
evaluations.rationale: Invitation mechanism (share URL) is specific enough to avoid multiple interpretations.

evaluations.evidence: start a round by entering an item in a single multi-line text field
evaluations.rationale: Defines the action and input UI element clearly; 'item' is consistently used as the thing being estimated.

evaluations.evidence: see all items we try to estimate this session
evaluations.rationale: The scope ('this session') and object ('all items') are clear; examples in the so-that clause do not introduce ambiguity.

evaluations.evidence: select an item to be estimated or re-estimated
evaluations.rationale: Selection target (an item) and effect (team sees that item and can estimate it) are clear.

evaluations.evidence: add an item to the list of items to be estimated
evaluations.rationale: Action and destination list are clear; no overloaded terms that change meaning.

evaluations.evidence: edit an item in the list of items to be estimated
evaluations.rationale: Editing an item in a list is a clear requirement without materially different interpretations.

evaluations.evidence: delete an item from the list of items to be estimated
evaluations.rationale: Delete operation and target are clear.

evaluations.evidence: show all estimates immediately
evaluations.rationale: “Immediately” is vague and can mean different triggers/timings (e.g., after moderator action, after each estimate, after some timeout), leading to materially different interpretations.

evaluations.evidence: accept the average of all estimates
evaluations.rationale: “Average” is ambiguous (mean vs median vs rounded mean; handling of non-numeric cards like '?', coffee; rounding rules), yielding different functional outcomes.

evaluations.evidence: filled in automatically if all estimators show the same card
evaluations.rationale: “Automatically” is unclear about when/how it happens (upon last card played, upon reveal, upon moderator action), which changes behavior materially.

evaluations.evidence: enter the agreed-upon estimate
evaluations.rationale: Moderator entering a final estimate is clear; “agreed-upon” refers to team agreement but does not create multiple system behaviors.

evaluations.evidence: estimate a story we estimated earlier in the session again
evaluations.rationale: Re-estimating a previously estimated story within the same session is clear.

evaluations.evidence: import stories from a spreadsheet
evaluations.rationale: “Spreadsheet” and “import” are underspecified (file type/format, required columns, mapping rules), allowing materially different interpretations of what is supported.

evaluations.evidence: copy/paste stories from a spreadsheet
evaluations.rationale: Ambiguous about what is pasted (cells/rows, plain text vs table), expected format, and how stories are parsed, leading to different implementations.

evaluations.evidence: browse through previous games
evaluations.rationale: “Browse through” is vague (list view, search, filters, pagination, ordering), enabling materially different interpretations of required functionality.

evaluations.evidence: view a transcript of a game
evaluations.rationale: “Transcript” is not defined (what events/fields are included: chat, timing, per-round details, participants), allowing different interpretations.

evaluations.evidence: export a transcript of a game as a HTML file
evaluations.rationale: Depends on ambiguous “transcript” content and also unclear HTML structure/contents, leading to different outputs.

evaluations.evidence: export a transcript of a game as a CSV file
evaluations.rationale: Depends on ambiguous “transcript” definition and unclear CSV schema (columns, row granularity), enabling materially different interpretations.

evaluations.evidence: delete a game, so that stories and estimates for this game are no longer stored
evaluations.rationale: Deletion target and intended data removal scope are stated clearly.

evaluations.evidence: create an account ... entering my name, email address, a password and a username
evaluations.rationale: Inputs and action are explicit; no materially different interpretations.

evaluations.evidence: log in using my account name and password
evaluations.rationale: “Account name” is ambiguous given PP-021 distinguishes email address and username; it could mean username or email, changing login behavior.

evaluations.evidence: change my account details
evaluations.rationale: “Account details” is underspecified (which fields: name, email, username, password, etc.), allowing materially different scopes.

evaluations.evidence: delete my account, so that account information and games are no longer stored
evaluations.rationale: Ambiguous scope of deletion (only owned games vs participated games; what constitutes “account information”), leading to different data-retention behaviors.

evaluations.evidence: see dates and times in my local timezone
evaluations.rationale: “Local timezone” is ambiguous (browser-detected vs profile setting; handling of travel/DST), which affects displayed times materially.

evaluations.evidence: get a password reminder by email
evaluations.rationale: “Password reminder” is ambiguous (send existing password vs reset link vs temporary password), which are materially different security/functional behaviors.

evaluations.evidence: select whether to have the team estimate with {0, 1/2, 1, 2, 3, 5, 8, etc.} or {0, 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32, etc.}
evaluations.rationale: Two concrete card sets are specified; the choice and intent are clear.

evaluations.evidence: invite up to 15 estimators
evaluations.rationale: Numeric limit is explicit and unambiguous.

evaluations.evidence: join a game by entering my name on the page I received the URL for
evaluations.rationale: Join mechanism (open URL, enter name) is clear.

evaluations.evidence: see the item we're estimating
evaluations.rationale: The object to display (current item being estimated) is clear in this domain context.

evaluations.evidence: see all items we will try to estimate this session
evaluations.rationale: Scope and object are clear; no materially different interpretations.

evaluations.evidence: immediately see that an estimate has been given
evaluations.rationale: “Immediately” is vague about timing/trigger (real-time push vs polling vs refresh), leading to different functional expectations.

evaluations.evidence: shown all estimates at the same time after all estimators have given their estimate
evaluations.rationale: Reveal condition (after all have estimated) and simultaneous display are clearly stated.

evaluations.evidence: change my estimate up until the last person selects a card and all are shown
evaluations.rationale: Defines a clear cutoff event for when changes are allowed.

evaluations.evidence: see each estimator's prior estimates for the story being estimated
evaluations.rationale: “Prior estimates” is ambiguous (prior rounds in same game vs across games; only this session vs historical), changing what data must be shown.

evaluations.evidence: see who gave what estimates during the current round
evaluations.rationale: Scope (“current round”) and mapping (estimator to estimate) are clear.

evaluations.evidence: be able start a two-minute countdown timer that all participants can see
evaluations.rationale: Ambiguous about who can start it (any participant vs specific roles), and what “start” entails if already running, leading to different behaviors.

evaluations.evidence: timer reset itself as soon as we all play an estimate
evaluations.rationale: “As soon as” is vague and “we all play an estimate” could mean when last card is selected vs when estimates are revealed, yielding different reset timing.

evaluations.evidence: scroll back through the stories and estimates from prior rounds
evaluations.rationale: “Scroll back through” is vague about UI/extent (within current game only vs across games; how far back; what is included), allowing different interpretations.

evaluations.evidence: always have the cards in the same order across multiple draws
evaluations.rationale: “Same order” is underspecified (what the canonical order is; whether configurable; how special cards are ordered), leading to different implementations.

evaluations.evidence: change my estimate as long as the draw has not been completed
evaluations.rationale: “Draw has not been completed” is ambiguous (completed when all have selected vs when revealed vs when moderator accepts), affecting when changes are allowed.

evaluations.evidence: have a small thumbnail photo displayed near where my cards are played
evaluations.rationale: Ambiguous about photo source (upload, gravatar, default), size/placement (“near where”), and whose photo is shown, leading to different UI/data requirements.

evaluations.evidence: compliant with XHTML and CSS standards
evaluations.rationale: “Compliant” and “standards” are ambiguous without specifying versions/levels and what constitutes compliance, allowing materially different interpretations.

evaluations.evidence: a list of definitions for commonly used terms
evaluations.rationale: “Commonly used terms” is vague (which terms, where used, completeness criteria), leading to different scopes for the list.

evaluations.evidence: created database indexes, so that the queries run as fast as possible
evaluations.rationale: “As fast as possible” is vague and “the queries” is underspecified (which queries), enabling materially different interpretations of what indexing is required.

evaluations.evidence: function correctly in Internet Explorer 6 and 7, Firefox 1.5 and 2, and Safari 2
evaluations.rationale: “Function correctly” is ambiguous (which features, acceptable degradation, layout vs functionality), allowing different interpretations of compatibility requirements.

evaluations.evidence: comply with the W3C accessibility guidelines where possible
evaluations.rationale: “Where possible” is vague and “W3C accessibility guidelines” is broad without specifying version/level (e.g., WCAG 2.0 AA), leading to multiple interpretations.

evaluations.evidence: respond quickly to my actions
evaluations.rationale: “Quickly” is subjective and can map to different performance thresholds, yielding materially different requirements.

evaluations.evidence: be able to use Unicode
evaluations.rationale: “Use Unicode” is underspecified (where: names, items, exports; which normalization/encoding; storage vs display), allowing different interpretations.

evaluations.evidence: see sensible and predictable URLs
evaluations.rationale: “Sensible and predictable” is subjective and can be interpreted in multiple materially different URL schemes.

evaluations.evidence: nice error pages when something goes wrong
evaluations.rationale: “Nice” and “something goes wrong” are vague (which errors, what content/design), enabling multiple interpretations.

evaluations.evidence: stored in a non-identifiable way
evaluations.rationale: “Non-identifiable” is ambiguous (anonymization vs pseudonymization; what identifiers are removed; re-identification risk threshold), leading to materially different data-handling requirements.

evaluations.evidence: see some metrics on use of the game
evaluations.rationale: “Some metrics” is vague (which metrics, time window, aggregation), allowing materially different interpretations of what must be provided.
